assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain the request path for a browser loading a page, from DNS resolution through the server response and browser rendering pipeline.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do front-end performance and correctness depend on network behavior, even when the application code itself appears sound?
key_evaluation_criteria: Knows the basic web request flow
Understands HTTP and networking terminology
Links browser behavior to end-user experience
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Trace a request step by step from browser to origin server and back; understanding the path usually reveals both performance and debugging issues.

nodes.name: HTML, CSS, and Semantic Layout Foundations

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Build a small responsive landing page using semantic HTML and CSS, and explain how your structure supports accessibility, responsiveness, and maintainability.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why can a visually attractive page still be poor user experience if the semantics and accessibility are weak?
key_evaluation_criteria: Uses semantic and accessible markup
Creates responsive, maintainable layout styles
Understands semantics and usability trade-offs
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Start by planning the content structure and the visual hierarchy, then implement the styles to support the intent rather than decorating arbitrarily.

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Create a small interactive UI that loads data from an API and updates the DOM safely when the user clicks or submits a form.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do async operations and event handlers often cause subtle bugs when variables, state, and timing are not managed carefully?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands core JS syntax and async behavior
Can manipulate DOM and handle events correctly
Builds dynamic UI logic without brittle code
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Separate data fetching, state updates, and rendering so each step stays testable and easier to reason about.

nodes.name: Version Control, Package Managers, and Tooling

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how you would structure a team project so that dependency updates, feature branches, and production releases remain safe and reviewable for front-end changes.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do small workflow inconsistencies in package management and version control often become expensive bottlenecks in a growing product team?
key_evaluation_criteria: Uses version control workflows correctly
Understands dependency and package tooling
Builds consistent project collaboration habits
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Keep branch and dependency management disciplined, because a strong workflow is as important as a strong UI in a team environment.

nodes.name: CSS Architecture, Utility Styling, and Design Systems
core_concepts: BEM, CSS Modules, and component styling
Design tokens and reusable UI systems

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how you would structure a multi-page product UI so that styling remains maintainable across components, teams, and design changes without creating CSS duplication or fragile overrides.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do large front-end codebases become difficult to scale when styles are tied to structure instead of design intent?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands scalable styling methods
Can articulate design-system principles
Chooses styling architecture based on codebase needs
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Prefer predictable, composable styling systems over one-off class overrides and ad hoc visual tweaks.

nodes.name: TypeScript, Tooling, and Frontend Build Systems
core_concepts: Tooling: Vite, Webpack, Rollup, esbuild, Parcel

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how TypeScript and a bundler improve developer velocity and reduction of production bugs in a medium-size front-end application.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why can a team sometimes ship smaller, fewer bugs, and better refactoring speed by choosing a typed system and well-tuned build pipeline?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands type safety and build tooling
Knows bundler trade-offs and developer ergonomics
Can explain why tooling choices affect reliability
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Use tooling to support maintainability and predictable builds; do not add layers of tooling without clear developer or runtime benefit.

nodes.name: Frontend Frameworks and Component Architecture
core_concepts: React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, and Solid principles

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Choose a front-end framework for a product with routing, complex shared state, and rapidly changing UI requirements, and explain your reasoning in terms of maintainability and developer productivity.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do framework choices matter less when a team is small and more when the app grows to multiple teams, features, and data flows?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands component architecture and state management
Can compare framework trade-offs meaningfully
Selects architecture based on product complexity
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Evaluate frameworks by the actual product constraints, not by hype, and prefer strong conventions over ad hoc decisions.

nodes.name: Testing, Quality Gates, and Frontend Reliability

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Design a testing strategy for a UI that includes authentication flows, form validation, and dynamic data updates, and explain which tests protect against regressions most effectively.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why is a front-end test suite only useful when it checks the behavior that users actually care about, not just component internals?
key_evaluation_criteria: Knows how to test different behavior layers
Understands regression prevention and CI quality gates
Builds confidence in user-visible interactions
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Use the smallest realistic test that captures user intent, and prefer real interactions over brittle implementation details where possible.

nodes.name: Web Security, Auth, and Browser Safety
core_concepts: CORS, HTTPS, CSP, and browser security model
JWT, OAuth, SSO, Basic Auth, session auth
Secure data handling and auth flows

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how you would secure a front-end application that calls a third-party API and needs user authentication without exposing tokens or allowing cross-site abuse.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do front-end security failures often come from trusting browser behavior too much, even when the app is technically correct?
key_evaluation_criteria: Knows browser security and auth trade-offs
Understands risk boundaries and API trust
Can propose secure patterns for sessions and tokens
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Security design starts with explicit trust boundaries and minimal privileges, not with final polishing or convenience at runtime.

nodes.name: Performance, Web APIs, and Browser Optimization
core_concepts: Service workers, notifications, storage, and device APIs

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: You are seeing poor performance on a product page with large assets and interactivity. Explain what measurements and browser tools you would use to identify the bottleneck and how you would improve the user experience.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do front-end performance issues often appear as a combination of network, rendering, and interaction bottlenecks rather than a single code defect?
key_evaluation_criteria: Knows how to measure and diagnose performance
Understands browser APIs and optimization opportunities
Can connect technical improvements to user experience
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Measure first and optimize the largest bottleneck with the highest user impact, rather than guessing based on anecdotal slowness.

nodes.name: SSR, SSG, and Modern Frontend Delivery Patterns
core_concepts: Routing, data fetching, and edge delivery

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: A product has both marketing pages and authenticated user pages. Explain how you would choose between client-only rendering, SSR, and static generation to balance speed, SEO, and user experience.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do the best rendering decisions depend on what the page is for, not just on the framework’s default behavior?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands different delivery models
Can align rendering strategy with product needs
Balances SEO, performance, and interactivity in design
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Choose the rendering model based on content freshness, interactivity, and SEO needs, then optimize the page accordingly.

nodes.name: Frontend Strategy, Product Craft, and Advanced Engineering

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Describe how you would scale a front-end platform across multiple teams while protecting performance, design consistency, and development velocity without strangling autonomy.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why does great front-end architecture require balancing product goals, team ergonomics, and long-term maintainability instead of optimizing only for short-term delivery speed?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands platform and product trade-offs
Can design scalable front-end engineering practices
Balances usability, quality, and velocity at organization level
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Use clear standards, reusable building blocks, and measurable quality goals so teams can move quickly without creating fragmented product experiences.
